topics.why_in_news: Indian Navy commissioned INS Anjadip, an Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC), to strengthen coastal defence and anti-submarine capabilities.
prelims_quick_notes: ASW-SWC designed for shallow-water anti-submarine operations.
Strengthens India’s coastal and maritime security architecture.
Anti-submarine warfare important for naval deterrence.
Craft equipped with sonar, torpedoes and rocket launchers.
Supports surveillance and protection of coastal waters.
Indian Navy modernising indigenous maritime capabilities.
Shallow-water crafts useful in littoral combat environments.
Maritime security critical for trade and energy security.
important_facts: SWC stands for Shallow Water Craft.
Built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE), Kolkata.
Uses waterjet propulsion for manoeuvrability and stealth.
Indian Ocean Region strategically important for global trade.
Maritime domain awareness essential for coastal security.
key_highlights: Focus on anti-submarine and surveillance operations.
Supports Atmanirbhar Bharat in defence manufacturing.
Improves operational readiness in littoral zones.
exam_relevance: Important for Internal Security, Defence and Maritime Security.
Useful for naval modernisation and indigenous defence topics.
Can be linked with Indo-Pacific strategy and coastal security.
prelims_traps: Shallow-water crafts designed specifically for littoral environments.
